newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CREDIT COMMUNAL IPO OVERSUBSCRIBED, CLOSES.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CREDIT COMMUNAL IPO OVERSUBSCRIBED, CLOSES.

text.p: The public share offer in Belgium's Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet van Belgie was heavily oversubscribed and will therefore end at the close of business on Tuesday, the offering banks said.
The offer of 3,212,507 shares in Credit Communal/ Gemeentekrediet had been due to close on Wednesday.
The effective price will be announced on November 20, the banks said in a statement, adding that allocation will be decided on objective criteria favouring small orders.
Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB), owned by local authorities, will be listed at a maximum price of 2,675 francs per share.
The 30 billion franc offering of up to 29.5 percent of the bank's shares opened for retail investors on November 8. Subscriptions for professional investors opened on November 4.

The listing is part of CCB's alliance with French Credit Local de France . CCB and CLF plan to join forces to create Europe's 22nd largest banking group, which will operate internationally under the name DEXIA.
CCB has applied to the Brussels Stock Exchange to be listed as DEXIA-CC from November 20.
